## Social movements & corporate brand  { visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

I think there is something to this surprise mechanism, but when I tried to test it against the alternative “legibility” hypothesis that those most familiar with the justice frame, not those to whom it would be surprising, were more likely to adopt it and change rule language. However, I also found that when this occurs, the policy is more likely to move, so I think the novelty is doing some work, just conditional on legibility. Happy to talk more about this. 

Attracting attention + fear of attention (p. 17) - Fire alarms are half the story. Happy to talk more about this.

Don't dismiss firms' brand management efforts. They might not always be as successful as they would like, but they are not widely boycotted. This type of PR is not what brokers typically do, but it does not mean that firms never do it. 

However, this all seems quite tangential to your intervention. As it stands, it is a lengthy digression, but in my opinion, not long enough to properly address public moral reputation management. 

## Structure  { visibility="uncounted"}

There are many digressions. You do a decent job of bringing the reader along with things like "returning to ...". Still. I think you want to 

1. set them apart with subheadings 
2. ask what role each serves and make sure it is tightly accomplishing that task
